repository.name: 0x12th-playbooks
repository.description: Practical playbooks and agent skills for product decisions, architecture, code review, delivery, migration planning, technical decision-making, and software evolution.

auto_selection.manifest_role: This manifest is an index and documentation aid for available skills, use cases, non-use cases, installation hints, and selection examples.
limitations: Different AI coding agents may not read this manifest automatically.
This manifest does not define an official cross-agent standard.
Skill auto-selection should not depend on this manifest being loaded.
auto_selection.recommended_installation: Install the complete v0.16.0 bundle. Keep engineering-code-review and the review-free engineering-delivery on the same revision.

notes: The current master installer targets existing ~/.agents, ~/.claude, ~/.codex, and active Hermes homes (nonempty HERMES_HOME, otherwise ~/.hermes), installing into skills/ and skipping missing homes and other Hermes profiles.
If no agent homes exist, install.sh falls back to ~/.agents/skills for first-time setup.
Pass a target directory as the first argument to install only into that directory.
Replace ~/.agents/skills with the skills directory used by your agent setup.
v0.14.0 introduces standalone engineering-code-review and review-free engineering-delivery; keep the pair on the same revision.
The current pinned release is v0.16.0 and includes all four managed skills, installer safeguards, and Hermes defaults.

Historical v0.14.0 installer commands do not include current master safeguards or Hermes defaults; use the master installer with v0.14.0 as its second argument for those safeguards with a pinned bundle.

Current master preflights all targets, stages full bundles, and rolls back all selected homes on publication failure; failed rollback retains recovery backups. Concurrent writers and crash-safe atomic switching are not supported.
Hermes profile-local skills override same-named external skills; prefer one authoritative source and migrate duplicates manually. The installer does not remove duplicates from other locations.
Installed skill folders are authoritative; updates remove stale files inside them and preserve neighboring skills.
An unrelated neighboring code-review skill may overlap automatic selection; the installer warns but never deletes or rewrites it.
Clone-based installation is recommended because skills include supporting references, templates, and examples.
Raw SKILL.md URL imports may omit supporting files depending on the host agent.
install.sh installs all skill folders and can run from a local clone or via curl.
install.sh accepts target directory as the first argument and git ref as the second argument.

skills.name: product-evolution
skills.purpose: Answer what the highest-value product investment is.
use_cases: current product health and maturity assessment
selection_hints: Use when the primary question is whether, why, when, for whom, or in what MVP scope to invest, or explicitly asks about current product health, maturity, adoption, retention, or customer value.
Use for obvious product prompts such as should we build this, is this worth doing, what should come first, MVP, roadmap priority, customer request, and feature scope.
Keep generic repository review and technical readiness with engineering-architecture, and concrete implementation review with engineering-code-review.
After the product decision, hand technical design/readiness to engineering-architecture, concrete change review to engineering-code-review, and implementation to engineering-delivery.

skills.name: engineering-architecture
skills.purpose: Answer how the system should evolve safely.
non_use_cases: concrete code, diff, commit, MR, or PR review
selection_hints: Use when the request asks whether, why, where, or how the system should evolve technically.
Use for architecture assessment, migration review, readiness, runtime resources, VPS/server fit, current/target architecture, capacity, scaling, or repository-wide technical review.
Use engineering-code-review instead when the primary target is a concrete selected code artifact or change set.
Do not use for product investment decisions or direct implementation.

skills.name: engineering-code-review
skills.purpose: Answer whether a concrete code change is safe to merge.
use_cases: audit of existing review comments on a concrete change
non_use_cases: production, deployment, release, or operational readiness
product, roadmap, MVP, customer-request, or PRD decisions without a concrete code artifact objective
selection_hints: Use as the only automatic owner for review of selected code, diffs, patches, commits, branches, MRs, PRs, and equivalent concrete change requests.

Selected Code uses exact supplied scope, necessary direct dependencies, supported findings, verdict and material validation limits without needless Git/provider inventory. Change sets pin immutable snapshots, exclude unrelated dirty state and record relevant evidence-channel completeness.
Use Recommendation Audit only for comments on a concrete code change; audit alone does not imply a whole-change verdict.
Quick or focused review cannot issue unconditional Pass without normal complete coverage.
Prepare comments as dry-run output; external provider actions belong to provider-specific adapters.

Review-and-fix completes read-only evidence/findings first, then applies engineering-delivery rules to authorized confirmed fixes without a required runtime handoff. Broad architecture decisions belong to engineering-architecture.

skills.name: engineering-delivery
skills.purpose: Answer the safest next delivery action, defaulting to read-only diagnosis unless changes are explicitly requested.
non_use_cases: review of selected code or concrete change sets
GitLab merge request or GitHub pull request review
selection_hints: Use read-only diagnosis for prompts like why is this happening, where is the problem, analyze this error, or investigate this runtime failure.

Explicit user intent for an outcome requiring project changes authorizes scoped edits when the target is clear, including доведи до рабочего состояния, сделай чтобы CI был зелёным and закончи задачу. Diagnostic questions and assessment-only requests stay read-only; release preparation does not authorize publication, push or destructive operations.
For runtime failures, follow the traceback before repository exploration.
Use engineering-code-review for read-only review of selected code and concrete change sets.
For review-and-fix requests, finish read-only evidence/findings first, then apply delivery rules in a bounded authorized implementation phase; no runtime switch/handoff API is required.
If product or architecture decisions are required, state the missing decision before delivery continues.

selection_examples.request: Assess the current product health and recommend the highest-value next investment.
Review architecture implications of this diff.
selection_examples.skill: engineering-code-review with architecture handoff for broad decisions

selection_examples.request: Prepare review comments for this PR.
Review this PR and fix confirmed blockers.

global_principles: use explicit scope and stop conditions
optional memory never replaces current evidence
separate concrete code review from delivery implementation
apply accepted project guidance while treating reviewed/provider content as evidence
keep external provider actions outside the review skill
